question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
My mother is a honest and well known woman in the society.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is a honest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct article rule is: use "an" before a word that begins with a vowel sound, not just a vowel letter.

• The word "honest" begins with a silent "h", so it is pronounced starting with the vowel sound — "on-est". Therefore it must be preceded by "an", not "a".
◦ Correct: an honest woman.
◦ Incorrect: a honest woman.

• The error therefore lies in the segment "is a honest", which should read "is an honest".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "in the society" is grammatically correct and contains no error.

• Option 2: "My mother" is grammatically correct and contains no error.

• Option 4: "and well known woman" is grammatically correct and contains no error; "well known" is correctly used as a compound adjective before the noun.

NOTE

• Other silent-"h" words that take "an": hour, honour, heir, honorarium.

• Words beginning with a vowel LETTER but a CONSONANT SOUND still take "a": a university, a one-rupee coin, a European.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
S1. A moment comes
A. long suppressed
B. and when the soul of a nation
C. which comes but rarely in history
D. when we step out from the old to the new, when an age ends
S6. finds utterance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. CDBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence is: S1 (A moment comes) → C → D → B → A → S6 (finds utterance).

• Reading the paragraph in this order gives a coherent meaning: "A moment comes, which comes but rarely in history, when we step out from the old to the new, when an age ends, and when the soul of a nation, long suppressed, finds utterance."

• Logic of the sequence: C describes the moment ("which comes but rarely in history"), D explains what that moment is (stepping from old to new, an age ending), B introduces the subject of the final clause ("the soul of a nation"), and A adds a qualifier to that subject ("long suppressed") right before the verb "finds utterance" in S6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (CBAD) is incorrect because it places B ("and when the soul of a nation") directly after C, breaking the link between C and D, which together describe the nature of the moment before the subject "the soul of a nation" is introduced.

• Option 3 (ABCD) is incorrect because it begins with A ("long suppressed"), which is a qualifier that must follow B ("the soul of a nation"), not precede the whole sequence.

• Option 4 (DCBA) is incorrect because it reverses C and D; D cannot logically follow C and precede B, since doing so disconnects the subject "the soul of a nation" from its verb "finds utterance" by inserting the qualifier chain in the wrong order.

NOTE

• In parajumble questions, always identify the sentence that logically must come immediately before the fixed last sentence (S6) — here, A ("long suppressed") must directly precede "finds utterance" since it qualifies "the soul of a nation".

• Look for grammatical links (pronouns, conjunctions like "and", "which") to chain sentences together correctly.

question: Identify the sentence that contains no spelling errors.
option_1: Manisha got overwhelmed by the tremendus offer by a company to work in collaboration with internet personel.
option_2: Manisha got overwhelmed by the tremendous offer by a company to work in collaboration with internet personnel.
option_3: Manisha got overwellmed by the tremendous offer by a company to work in collaborasion with internet personnel.
option_4: Manisha got overwhelmed by the tremendous offer by a company to work in collaborasion with internet personnal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Manisha got overwhelmed by the tremendous offer by a company to work in collaboration with internet personnel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Option 2 is the only sentence in which all four tested words are spelt correctly: "overwhelmed", "tremendous", "collaboration" and "personnel".

• Spelling key: overwhelmed has a single "l" after "whe"; tremendous ends in -dous, not -dus; collaboration has a single "b" and ends -ation, not -asion; personnel (meaning staff/employees) ends -nnel, and must not be confused with personal (meaning private/individual) or misspelt as personel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because of two spelling errors: "tremendus" (should be "tremendous") and "personel" (should be "personnel").

• Option 3 is incorrect because of two spelling errors: "overwellmed" (should be "overwhelmed") and "collaborasion" (should be "collaboration").

• Option 4 is incorrect because of two spelling errors: "collaborasion" (should be "collaboration") and "personnal" (should be "personnel" — this option confuses "personnel" with "personal").

NOTE

• Commonly confused pair: personnel (staff of an organisation) vs personal (private, relating to oneself).

• Words ending in -tion are frequently mis-spelt with -sion by candidates; always check whether the base word takes "t" or "s" before the ending (e.g., collaboration, information, education — all "-tion"; decision, division, confusion — all "-sion").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
In a soup
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. In trouble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "In a soup" means to be in a difficult, confusing or troublesome situation. (मुसीबत में)
◦ Example: He landed in a soup when he lost the company's confidential documents.

• The idiom draws on the image of being immersed in something thick and messy, just like being stuck in a difficult situation with no easy way out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To be extremely short of money (पैसे की कमी होना) is actually the meaning of idioms like "to be in the red" or "to be strapped for cash", not "in a soup".

• Option 2: To exhibit cowardice (कायरता दिखाना) is the meaning of idioms like "to show the white feather", not "in a soup".

• Option 3: To get nothing (कुछ नहीं मिलना) is the meaning of idioms like "to draw a blank", not "in a soup".

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "in trouble" often asked in SSC: "In hot water", "In a fix", and "In a pickle".

• Do not confuse "in a soup" (trouble) with a similar-sounding phrase — the fixed idiomatic form is always "in a soup", not "in the soup".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
They praised her for her bravery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rebuked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "praised" means to express approval or admiration for someone. (प्रशंसा करना)

• Its antonym is "Rebuked", which means to express sharp disapproval or criticism of someone. (डांटना/भर्त्सना करना)
◦ Example: The teacher rebuked the student for arriving late every day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Acclaimed" means to praise enthusiastically or publicly approve of, which is a synonym, not an antonym, of "praised".

• Option 3: "Defended" means to support or protect someone against criticism; it is related to praise in spirit but does not mean the opposite of "praised".

• Option 4: "Assaulted" means to physically attack someone; it is not related to verbal approval or disapproval, so it cannot be the antonym of "praised".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "praise": commend, laud, extol, applaud.

• Other antonyms of "praise": criticise, condemn, denounce, censure, reprimand.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Intentional
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Unplanned.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Intentional" means done deliberately or on purpose. (जानबूझकर किया गया)

• Its antonym is "Unplanned", which means not planned in advance, done without deliberate intention. (अनियोजित/अनजाने में)
◦ Example: The mistake in the report was completely unplanned.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Cordial" means warm and friendly; it is unrelated to the idea of intention or purpose.

• Option 3: "Amiable" means friendly and pleasant in nature; like "cordial", it has no connection to the meaning of "intentional".

• Option 4: "Inanimate" means not alive or lacking life, which is unrelated to the concept of doing something deliberately.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "intentional": deliberate, calculated, premeditated, wilful.

• Other antonyms of "intentional": accidental, unintentional, inadvertent, involuntary.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Abandon
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Continue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Abandon" means to give up or leave something completely, often permanently. (छोड़ देना/त्याग देना)

• Its antonym is "Continue", which means to keep doing something without stopping. (जारी रखना)
◦ Example: Despite the difficulties, the team decided to continue the project instead of abandoning it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Quit" means to stop or leave something, which is a synonym, not an antonym, of "abandon".

• Option 2: "Surrender" means to give up or yield, which is also close in meaning to "abandon" and therefore not its antonym.

• Option 3: "Shorten" means to make something shorter in length or duration; it has no direct opposite relationship with "abandon".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "abandon": desert, forsake, relinquish, renounce.

• Other antonyms of "abandon": maintain, persist, retain, preserve.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. The 1995 World Summit for Social Development had also emphasised the pivotal role of women in eradicating poverty and mending the social fabric.
B. Women are rational in approach, careful in handling situations and want to do things as best as possible.
C. The Fourth World Conference of Women held in Beijing in September 1995 had emphasised that no enduring solution of society's most threatening social, economic and political problems could be found without the participation and empowerment of the women.
D. Today's woman is a highly self-directed person, alive to the sense of her dignity and the importance of her functions in the private domestic domain and the public domain of the world of work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DBCA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence is D → B → C → A, which reads: "Today's woman is a highly self-directed person... Women are rational in approach... The Fourth World Conference of Women held in Beijing in September 1995 had emphasised... The 1995 World Summit for Social Development had ALSO emphasised the pivotal role of women..."

• Logic of the sequence: D introduces the topic (today's woman as self-directed), B adds a related general observation about women's rational approach, C cites a specific international event (the Beijing conference) supporting the idea, and A follows naturally by citing a second, related event using the word "also", which signals that a similar point was made just before — linking back to sentence C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (ABDC) is incorrect because it begins with A, which contains the word "also" — a word that only makes sense after another similar point (such as sentence C) has already been made, so A cannot be the first sentence.

• Option 3 (DBAC) is incorrect because it places A before C; since A says the World Summit had "also" emphasised the same point, the Beijing Conference (C) must be mentioned before A, not after.

• Option 4 (BCAD) is incorrect because it starts with B, but there is no earlier reference established for "Women are rational in approach..." to logically open the paragraph before the broader introductory idea in D is presented.

NOTE

• A word like "also", "too", or "similarly" at the start of a sentence is a strong clue that the sentence cannot be the first sentence of the paragraph — it must follow a sentence making a related point.

• Always look for such linking words (also, however, therefore, this) to establish sequence in parajumbles.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
Being a practiced liar, it was totally normal for him to utter a complete and blatant lie.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. falsehood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "complete and blatant lie" means an obvious, shameless untruth. The single word that best substitutes this meaning is "falsehood", which means a lie or an untrue statement. (झूठ/असत्य कथन)
◦ Example: The politician's falsehood was exposed by the journalist within a day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Blasphemy" (ईश्वर-निंदा) means irreverent or disrespectful speech about God or sacred things; it has nothing to do with lying.

• Option 2: "Whooper" is not a standard English word with a relevant meaning here ("whopper" — note the different spelling — informally means "a big lie", but "whooper" as printed is a distractor, not a valid substitute).

• Option 4: "Perjury" (शपथ के विरुद्ध झूठी गवाही) specifically means lying under oath in a court of law; the given sentence has no legal or courtroom context, so it does not fit.

NOTE

• Related words for "lie": fabrication, fib, deceit, untruth, prevarication.

• Do not confuse "falsehood" (a lie, general) with "perjury" (a lie under legal oath, a specific legal term).

question:
Select the option that contains a grammatical error in the underlined portion.
He was always been a grumpy man so I never liked him and avoided his company.
option_1: He was always been a grumpy man, __so I never liked him__ and avoided his company.
option_2: __He was always been__ a grumpy man, so I never liked him and avoided his company.
option_3: He was always been __a grumpy man__, so I never liked him and avoided his company.
option_4: He was always been a grumpy man, so I never liked him __and avoided his company__.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. "He was always been" (underlined portion).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined portion "He was always been" contains the grammatical error. The structure "was...been" incorrectly combines the Simple Past tense auxiliary "was" with the past participle "been", which is not a valid tense form in English.

• Rule: To describe a state that continued over a period up to a point in the past, the correct structure is the Past Perfect tense: Subject + had + been + complement, i.e., "He had always been a grumpy man."

• Applying the rule, the correct sentence should read: "He had always been a grumpy man, so I never liked him and avoided his company."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 underlines "so I never liked him", which is grammatically correct — a simple past tense clause correctly connected with "so".

• Option 3 underlines "a grumpy man", which is simply a noun phrase used correctly as the complement and contains no grammatical error.

• Option 4 underlines "and avoided his company", which is a correctly formed simple past tense verb phrase parallel to "liked", and contains no grammatical error.

NOTE

• A common SSC error type mixes an auxiliary verb of one tense with the participle of another (e.g., "was...been", "has...was") — always check that the auxiliary and the main verb form belong to the same, valid tense.

• Remember the fixed structures: Simple Past — was/were + V1; Present Perfect — has/have + V3; Past Perfect — had + V3 (never "was + been").

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A person who does not drink alcohol.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Teetotaller.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Teetotaller" is a person who never drinks alcohol / abstains completely from alcoholic drinks. (शराब न पीने वाला व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: Being a strict teetotaller, he refused the glass of wine offered at the party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Vegetarian" (शाकाहारी) refers to a person who does not eat meat, which is unrelated to drinking alcohol.

• Option 2: "Celibate" (ब्रह्मचारी) refers to a person who abstains from marriage or sexual relations, not from alcohol.

• Option 4: "Abstain" is a verb meaning to deliberately not do something; it is not a noun describing a person, so it cannot function as the one-word substitute here.

NOTE

• Other useful one-word substitutes involving abstinence: Ascetic (one who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from worldly pleasures), Vegan (one who eats no animal products at all).

• Do not confuse "teetotaller" (no alcohol at all) with a "moderate drinker" (drinks alcohol in small amounts).

question: Describe how you will tell your parents that Suraj is loved by Siva in active voice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Siva loves Suraj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Suraj is loved by Siva" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Present Tense (Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject).

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "Siva" (after "by") becomes the subject; since "Siva" is third person singular, the verb takes "-s", so "love" becomes "loves"; and "Suraj" (the earlier subject) becomes the object.
◦ Active: Siva loves Suraj.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is been loving" is not a valid active-voice verb form; it wrongly mixes the passive auxiliary "is been" with the continuous form.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "loved" is the Simple Past tense form, whereas the original sentence is in the Simple Present tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "were loving" is a Past Continuous form, and it also wrongly uses the plural auxiliary "were" with the singular subject "Siva".

NOTE

• When converting Passive to Active, always identify the subject after "by" first — that becomes the new subject — and match the verb tense and person/number correctly with the new subject.

• The tense of the sentence never changes in Active–Passive conversion, only the subject–object arrangement and the verb form.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pronounciation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Pronunciation", not "Pronounciation" — note that although the related verb is "pronounce" (with "ou"), the noun form drops the "o" and is spelt pro-nun-ci-a-tion. (उच्चारण)
◦ Example: Her pronunciation of French words was nearly perfect.

• Spelling key: PRO + NUN + CI + A + TION — remember there is no "ou" in the noun form, unlike in the verb "pronounce".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Believe" is correctly spelt — remember the rule "i before e except after c": believe has no "c" before it, so "ie" is used.

• Option 2: "Audible" is correctly spelt, meaning able to be heard.

• Option 3: "Throat" is correctly spelt, referring to the front part of the neck.

NOTE

• Other word-pairs where the noun form drops a letter present in the verb form: pronounce → pronunciation; similarly, be careful with maintain → maintenance and describe → description.

• Commonly misspelt SSC words: rhythm, occurrence, questionnaire, embarrass, accommodate.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
I confronted the journalist with the evidence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Avoided.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "confronted" means to face or meet someone directly, especially in a challenging way. (सामना करना)

• Its antonym is "Avoided", which means to keep away from or stay clear of someone or something. (टालना/बचना)
◦ Example: Instead of confronting the issue, he avoided the journalist altogether.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Resisted" means to oppose or withstand something; it is related to confrontation in spirit and is not its opposite.

• Option 3: "Challenged" means to dispute or question something directly, which is close in meaning to "confronted", not its opposite.

• Option 4: "Encountered" means to meet or come across someone, often unexpectedly, which is a synonym, not an antonym, of "confronted".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "confront": face, defy, tackle.

• Other antonyms of "confront": evade, dodge, shun, elude.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the given group of words.
The better you know someone the less you like him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Familiarity breeds contempt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Familiarity breeds contempt" means the more closely and frequently you know someone, the more likely you are to notice their faults and lose respect or liking for them — exactly matching "the better you know someone the less you like him". (अधिक जान-पहचान से आदर घट जाता है)
◦ Example: After sharing a room for months, the two friends started irritating each other — familiarity breeds contempt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Save for a rainy day" (मुसीबत के लिए बचत करना) means to save money or resources for a time of future need; it has no connection with liking or disliking someone.

• Option 2: "Spill the beans" (राज़़ खोलना) means to reveal a secret; it is unrelated to the given meaning.

• Option 3: "The elephant in the room" (नज़रअंदाज़ की गई स्पष्ट समस्या) means an obvious problem that everyone avoids discussing; it does not match the given meaning about familiarity and liking.

NOTE

• Other idioms about relationships/human nature often asked in SSC: "Absence makes the heart grow fonder" (missing someone increases affection), "Blood is thicker than water" (family bonds are stronger than others).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Prohibition
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Permission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Prohibition" means the act of formally forbidding something by law or rule. (निषेध/प्रतिबंध)

• Its antonym is "Permission", which means the act of formally allowing something. (अनुमति)
◦ Example: The government lifted the prohibition and granted permission for the event to be held.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Restriction" means a limitation placed on something, which is close in meaning to "prohibition", not its opposite.

• Option 2: "Inhibition" means a feeling that makes one self-conscious or holds one back; it is related to restraint, similar in sense to "prohibition", not opposite.

• Option 3: "Direction" means guidance or instruction on how to do something; it is unrelated to the concept of forbidding or allowing.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "prohibition": ban, embargo, veto, interdiction.

• Other antonyms of "prohibition": authorisation, sanction, approval, consent.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The French had regarded the scholar as a usurper.
option_1: The scholar was being regarded as a usurper by the French.
option_2: The scholar has been regarded as a usurper by the French.
option_3: The scholar was regarded as a usurper by the French.
option_4: The scholar had been regarded as a usurper by the French.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The scholar had been regarded as a usurper by the French.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The French had regarded the scholar as a usurper" is in the Active Voice, Past Perfect Tense (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

• Rule — Past Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + had + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the scholar" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "had been" is used; the verb "regarded" (already V3) remains "regarded"; and "the French" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: The scholar had been regarded as a usurper by the French.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was being regarded" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Past Perfect Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "has been regarded" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense, not the Past Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "was regarded" is the passive form of the Simple Past Tense, not the Past Perfect Tense.

NOTE

• Always match the auxiliary in the passive sentence to the exact tense of the active sentence — "had" signals Past Perfect and requires "had been + V3" in the passive, never "was/has been".

• Fixed passive structures: Simple Past — was/were + V3; Present Perfect — has/have been + V3; Past Perfect — had been + V3.

question:
Select the most appropriate word segment for the underlined word in the given sentence.
Pintu has been advised to reduce smoking by his family doctor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. cut down.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "reduce" means to make something smaller in amount or degree. In the context of habits like smoking, the standard phrasal verb used is "cut down (on)", meaning to decrease the amount of something one does or consumes. (कम करना)
◦ Example: The doctor advised him to cut down on smoking for better health.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "lower down" is not an idiomatic phrasal verb used with habits like smoking; "lower" is typically used for physical position or level (e.g., lower down the volume), not for reducing a habit in this natural way.

• Option 2: "up down" is not a meaningful or grammatically valid phrase in English.

• Option 3: "less down" is not a standard English phrase; "less" is not combined with "down" in this way.

NOTE

• Common phrasal verbs of reduction tested in SSC: cut down (on) — reduce consumption of something; cut back (on) — similar meaning, reduce spending or usage; scale down — reduce the size or extent of something.

• Do not confuse "cut down" (reduce) with "cut off" (disconnect/stop supply) or "cut out" (stop doing something completely, e.g., "cut out smoking entirely").

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Something belonging to or surviving from an earlier period
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Relic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Relic" is an object, custom, or belief that has survived from an earlier time, especially one of historical interest. (प्राचीन काल की वस्तु/अवशेष)
◦ Example: The museum displayed several relics from the Mughal era.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Vestige" means the last small remaining trace of something that once existed, focusing on a faint or barely perceptible remainder, rather than a surviving object of the earlier period itself.

• Option 2: "Dinosaur" refers to a prehistoric reptile (or informally, someone/something outdated); it is not a general term for "something surviving from an earlier period".

• Option 3: "Ruin" refers to the remains of a destroyed or decayed structure; it specifically implies destruction or decay, not simply "belonging to or surviving from" an earlier time.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Antique (an object valued for its age, typically over 100 years old), Heirloom (a valuable object passed down through generations of a family).

• Do not confuse "relic" (a surviving object of historical value) with "vestige" (a faint trace or remnant, not necessarily a tangible object).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The internationally agreed Declaration of the Small Island Developing States (SIDS) Accelerated Modalities of Action, the so-called S.A.M.O.A Pathway, recognises that SIDS remains a special case for sustainable development in view of their unique and particular vulnerabilities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. imperishable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "sustainable" means able to be maintained or continued at a certain level over time, especially without depleting resources or causing lasting harm. (टिकाउ/स्थायी)

• Among the given options, "imperishable", meaning enduring, lasting, not liable to decay or come to an end, is the closest in sense to "sustainable", since both convey the idea of something continuing or lasting over time.
◦ Example: The report calls for imperishable, long-term solutions to environmental vulnerabilities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "vast" means very large in area or extent; it has no connection with the idea of something lasting or being maintained over time.

• Option 2: "unsuitable" means not fitting or appropriate for a purpose; this is essentially opposite in sense to what "sustainable" conveys in this context.

• Option 3: "rare" means not common or infrequent; it does not relate to the idea of continuity or endurance implied by "sustainable".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "sustainable" in different contexts: viable, maintainable, renewable, enduring.

• Antonyms of "sustainable": unsustainable, perishable, unviable, temporary.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the 19th century, there was an industrial revolution in Europe. As a result, millions of people left the (1)________ and went to work in big factories in cities. Today, it is the reverse. In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2)________environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3)________, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Beside, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4)________to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5)________, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. villages.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage describes the 19th century Industrial Revolution, during which people moved from rural areas to work in factories in cities. The word that fits blank (1) must refer to the place people left to go and work in cities — that is, "villages".

• The sentence reads: "millions of people left the villages and went to work in big factories in cities", which correctly describes the historical rural-to-urban migration pattern of the Industrial Revolution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "cities" is incorrect because the sentence already states that people went TO work in cities; they cannot have left cities to go to cities.

• Option 2: "colonies" is incorrect because the passage is about internal rural-to-urban migration within Europe, not about people leaving colonies.

• Option 4: "countries" is incorrect because it is too broad; the specific and logical contrast in the passage is between "villages" (rural) and "cities" (urban), not between different countries.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the full sentence and surrounding context (not just the blank) to identify the logical contrast or relationship the sentence is building — here, the village-to-city migration.

• Common paired contrasts tested in SSC cloze passages: rural/urban, rise/fall, cause/effect.

• Option 4: "higher" is incorrect because "higher" does not relate meaningfully to the quality of an environment in this context.

NOTE

In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2)________environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3)________, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Beside, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4)________to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5)________, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Instead.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank connects two contrasting ideas: "there are fewer jobs in 'heavy' industries like steel and power generation" and "there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery". The connector must show that service-industry jobs are replacing heavy-industry jobs, which is exactly the meaning of "Instead".

• Rule: "Instead" is used to indicate that one thing is being replaced by or substituted with another, which precisely captures the shift described from heavy industry jobs to service industry jobs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Of course" is incorrect because it is used to express agreement or something obviously true, not to show a replacement relationship between two contrasting facts.

• Option 3: "Clearly" is incorrect because it is used to emphasise that something is evident, not to indicate substitution or replacement.

• Option 4: "Nevertheless" is incorrect because it is used to show contrast despite something (similar to "however"), but here the relationship is not one of contradiction — it is one of substitution/replacement, which "Instead" captures more precisely.

NOTE

• Distinguish connector meanings carefully: "Instead" = in place of; "Nevertheless/However" = in spite of, contrast; "Therefore" = as a result, consequence.

• SSC cloze passages frequently test the correct connector by requiring you to understand the logical relationship (cause-effect, contrast, addition, substitution) between two clauses.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. commute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank fits into the phrase "made it easier for people to (4)________ to work or even work from home". The word "commute" means to travel regularly between one's home and place of work, which fits precisely with "to work" following the blank.

• The sentence reads: "modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to commute to work or even work from home", contrasting commuting to a workplace with the alternative of working from home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3: "communicate" means to exchange information; while modern communications are mentioned in the passage, the blank specifically follows "to work", which requires a verb about travelling to a workplace, not exchanging messages.

• Option 4: "calculate" means to work out a number or amount mathematically; it has no relevance to travelling to work.

NOTE

• "Commute to work" is a fixed, commonly tested collocation meaning to travel to one's workplace regularly.

• Do not confuse "commute" (to travel to work) with "communicate" (to exchange information) — both begin similarly but have very different meanings.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. outwards.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase describing "spread cities": "cities are growing fast, but (5)________, away from city centres". The word "outwards" means moving away from a central point in an outward direction, which matches "away from city centres" perfectly.

• The sentence reads: "cities are growing fast, but outwards, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away", describing cities expanding in area away from their centres rather than growing vertically or in population density at the centre.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "downward" is incorrect because it suggests movement in a vertical, descending direction, which does not match the idea of spreading away from a city centre.

• Option 3: "upward" is incorrect because it suggests vertical, ascending growth (like tall buildings), which contradicts the passage's description of "spread cities" expanding outward, not upward.

• Option 4: "inward" is incorrect because it means moving toward the centre, which is the exact opposite of the passage's description of people moving "away from city centres".

NOTE

• The direction word must always be checked against its accompanying phrase for logical consistency — here "away from city centres" directly supports "outwards" and rules out "inward".

• Common directional word sets tested in SSC: inward/outward, upward/downward, forward/backward.
